clue.text: Violets, main variety of this garden bloomer

indicators.note: a variety of the letters means they are rearranged into a new order here

explanation.surface: A gardener admires a striking display of violets in the main bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variety' sounds horticultural but tells you to rearrange VIOLETS and MAIN into the plant's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Love-in-a-mist is a nigella, a blue-flowered annual grown in cottage gardens.

clue.text: Voting without a leader in Reading, say?

indicators.note: losing the leader means the first letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: voting is an election

explanation.surface: A by-election in the town of Reading is held with no candidate leading.
explanation.walkthrough: Reading is the Berkshire town in the surface, but here it means a passage read aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: A lection is a passage of scripture read out in church, a reading.

clue.text: Sells goods-knocks off at five

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five
to knock off work is to end it, giving ends

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper sells goods and knocks off at five o'clock.
explanation.definitionFit: To vend is to sell, especially small goods from a stall or machine.

clue.text: Quick to get in hot Carib isle, possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A traveller is quick to arrive on a hot Caribbean island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quick to get in hot' means quick to get into a temper, not quick to arrive somewhere warm.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone irascible is hot-tempered, easily roused to anger.

clue.text: Alliance records a big hit on the way back

indicators.note: travelling on the way back means the word is written backwards

parts.note: a six is the biggest hit in cricket, clearing the boundary

explanation.surface: A political alliance records a big electoral success while heading home.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a six is a hit over the boundary without bouncing. 'records' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Axis was the wartime alliance of Germany, Italy and Japan.

clue.text: Craft needed to tack on cold sheets?

definitions.text: Craft needed to tack on cold sheets?

parts.words: Craft needed to tack on cold sheets?
parts.note: sheets sound like bedding or sails' ropes, but here they are frozen sheets of ice a sailing craft runs over on runners

explanation.surface: Someone needs a craft to make tacks while lying in cold bed sheets.
explanation.definitionFit: An ice yacht is a sail-driven vessel on runners that tacks across frozen lakes.

clue.text: Initially turkey roulade is unacceptable-try the fish!

indicators.note: initially means take the opening letter of each of the next words

parts.note: something out is not acceptable, as in 'that idea is out'

explanation.surface: A diner rejects the turkey roulade and is urged to try the fish instead.
explanation.definitionFit: Trout is a freshwater fish of the salmon family.

clue.text: Empty day-unpleasant for the line of leaders

indicators.note: emptying a word removes its insides, keeping its first and last letters

parts.note: nasty means unpleasant

explanation.surface: A ruler has a dull, unpleasant day of leadership.
explanation.definitionFit: A dynasty is a succession of rulers from one family.

clue.text: China Dog?

parts.note: read as a porcelain ornament, but it means a breed of dog from China, named after its old capital

explanation.surface: A china ornament shaped like a dog.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pekinese is a small long-haired toy breed from Peking, now Beijing.

clue.text: In singing style of Cambridge University, first half of Elijah is set back

parts.note: Cantab is the abbreviation for Cambridge University, from Latin Cantabrigiensis

indicators.note: set back means the letters are written in reverse
the first half of the word means its opening three of six letters

explanation.surface: A Cambridge choir performs the first half of Mendelssohn's Elijah in its own style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set back' turns ELI, the first half of 'Elijah', into ILE.
explanation.definitionFit: Cantabile is a musical direction to play smoothly in a song-like manner.

clue.text: Theatre circle done to order

parts.note: a circle is the shape of the letter O

indicators.note: done to order means rearranged as required

explanation.surface: The theatre's dress circle has been redone to customers' wishes.
explanation.definitionFit: Odeon is a chain of British cinemas, and originally a hall for performance.

clue.text: Insignificant creature in the church group

parts.note: a sect is a breakaway religious group

explanation.surface: Someone feels like an insignificant creature within the church congregation.
explanation.definitionFit: A bug or beetle is a tiny creature of little importance.

clue.text: Dad's attempts to make vol-au-vents?

parts.note: pa's means belonging to dad
tries are attempts

explanation.surface: Father keeps trying to make vol-au-vents for a party.
explanation.definitionFit: Vol-au-vents are puff-pastry cases, an example of baked pastry goods.

clue.text: Barney"-novel close at hand

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters take a fresh order

explanation.surface: A novel titled Barney is lying close at hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Something close at hand is a short distance away.

clue.text: Pure sovereign?

definitions.meaning: unmixed, complete, as in utter nonsense
a ruler with unlimited power, as in an autocratic monarch

explanation.definitionFit: Absolute means unadulterated, and an absolute monarch rules with no constitutional limits.

clue.text: Hard lines following fate in court

annotationWithheld.why: Hard lines following fate in court (8): CHANCE (fate) + RY (lines) gives the answer, but no job can be found for 'Hard'; the clue as held may be misread
annotationWithheld.clue: Hard lines following fate in court

clue.text: The late shift?

parts.note: reads as a night's work at a factory, but a shift is also a loose garment worn late at night

explanation.surface: Workers clock on for the late shift.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightdress is a loose garment, once called a shift, worn in bed.

clue.text: Endlessly Gallic, I do change the flowers

indicators.note: change tells you to put these letters in a different order
endlessly means the last letter of the word is removed

explanation.surface: A Frenchman endlessly changing the flower arrangement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endlessly' cuts 'Gallic' to GALLI; 'change' rearranges GALLI, I, DO.
explanation.definitionFit: Gladioli are tall plants with sword-shaped leaves and spikes of blooms.

clue.text: Made false start at Newmarket (traffic caught in fog)

indicators.note: caught in means placed inside the other word

parts.note: mist is a thin fog
to traffic is to deal, trade

explanation.surface: A jockey made a false start at Newmarket racecourse after being delayed in fog.
explanation.walkthrough: Newmarket is a racecourse in Suffolk, but it is also a card game: a false start there is a bad deal of the cards.
explanation.definitionFit: To misdeal is to distribute cards wrongly, botching the start of a hand.

clue.text: Hot-stuff celebrity in the dirt

indicators.note: in places the celebrity inside the dirt

parts.note: mud is wet dirt
a star is a celebrity

explanation.surface: A famous person ends up in the mud of tabloid gossip.
explanation.definitionFit: English mustard is a pungent yellow condiment that burns the tongue.

clue.text: Eager to change old penny, settled

indicators.note: to change means the letters are reorganised

parts.note: d was the abbreviation for a penny before British decimal currency

explanation.surface: Someone eager to swap an old penny settles the deal.
explanation.definitionFit: A matter agreed is one decided and settled between parties.

clue.text: Did charitable acts in London, at Edgware

indicators.note: in signals that the letters are found inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Volunteers performed good deeds in London, at Edgware.
explanation.walkthrough: Edgware is a district of north London.
explanation.definitionFit: To donate is to give money or goods to a good cause.

clue.text: Sporting loud ties leads to isolation

indicators.note: sporting means wearing, displaying, here showing the letters in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Wearing loud ties leaves a man shunned by colleagues.
explanation.definitionFit: Solitude is the state of being alone, apart from others.

clue.text: Doctor's first note?

definitions.meaning: what a doctor prescribes, a pick-me-up medicine
the keynote of a musical scale, its first degree

explanation.definitionFit: A tonic is a restorative medicine, and the tonic is the first note of a major or minor scale.

clue.text: Family tune?

definitions.meaning: a line of descent or breed, as in a variety
a melody or snatch of music

explanation.definitionFit: A strain is a breed or lineage, and strains of music are melodies.

clue.text: Quick and active

definitions.meaning: living, as in the quick and the dead

explanation.definitionFit: Quick in its old sense means living, and lively means full of energy.

clue.text: Scorn counterfeit

definitions.meaning: imitation or sham, as in a fake Tudor house

explanation.definitionFit: To deride is to ridicule, and sham items are imitations of the real thing.

clue.text: Variety turn appearing in London district

parts.note: an act is a performer's turn in a variety show
on means appearing on stage

explanation.surface: A music-hall turn is performing in a London district.
explanation.walkthrough: Acton is a district of west London.
explanation.definitionFit: Acton is a suburb in west London, in the borough of Ealing.

clue.text: Clockmaker lost head, to become mountain-mapper

indicators.note: losing its head means the word drops its first letter

parts.note: a horologist makes clocks and watches

explanation.surface: A clockmaker loses his mind and becomes a mapper of mountains.
explanation.definitionFit: Orology is the scientific study of mountains, so its student describes and charts them.

clue.text: Not much money put down in poultry-farm

definitions.meaning: grain scattered on the ground for the hens

explanation.definitionFit: A paltry amount is called by this name, and literally it is grain fed to hens.
